# Fever, colds and flu in adults

A one-page summary from the clinic's patient portal, saved for the winter.

## When an adult should call a doctor

Call the doctor for a fever of 103°F (39.4°C) or higher, or for any fever that lasts more than 3 days. Get care the same day for a stiff neck, confusion, trouble breathing, chest pain, or a fever that comes back after you seemed to be getting better.

## Cold or flu?

A cold comes on gradually with a stuffy nose, sneezing and a sore throat, and rarely a high fever. Flu hits fast: fever, chills, body aches and exhaustion, often with a dry cough. Flu is the one that can put you in bed for a week.

## Treating flu at home

Rest, drink plenty of fluids, and use acetaminophen or ibuprofen as directed on the label for aches and fever. An antiviral prescription works best when started within 48 hours of the first symptoms, so call early if you are over 65, pregnant, or have asthma, diabetes or heart disease.

## Is it a sinus infection?

Most sinus trouble is viral and clears on its own. Think about a bacterial infection when symptoms last more than 10 days without improving, or when you get better and then suddenly worse. Antibiotics do nothing for a viral infection.

## When to stay home

Stay home until you have been fever-free for 24 hours without fever-reducing medicine and your symptoms are improving. Cover coughs and wash your hands often for the first week.
